text:
Maya K: paging oncall — alert: policy-engine panicked, smart-routing started spamming fallbacks 

sre-bot: [incident created] incident_id=INC-20240427-874, severity=sev2, resource=policy-engine-prod-1, alerted: @Maya K, @Liam W

Maya K: seeing a cascade — requests keep getting routed to a fallback variant (small-quantized) and then immediately re-routed back, causing regional capacity spikes. customers reporting elevated 502s and timeouts.

Liam W: I can join. attaching the latest tail of policy-engine logs. stack trace looks like a panic during rule eval.

Liam W: ```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
  goroutine 2345 [running]:
github.com/redwood/policy.evalRule(
  /srv/repo/policy/evaluator.go:78 +0x1b2
)
main.main.func1(
  /srv/repo/cmd/policy/main.go:43 +0x45
)
...
error: expression "request.user_tier == "enterprise" && route.region in ["us", "eu"]" failed: invalid operator 'in' on non-list
```

Arjun Patel: that expression was recently shipped in the latest routing rules rollout from yesterday — I remember a hurried patch to support region lists. looks like the parser accepted an invalid AST and eval crashed when it hit a nil.

Maya K: immediate mitigation options? can we disable the policy engine and fail-open to simple cost-based routing?

Liam W: yes. two options: (A) flip feature-flag policy-eval=off in the runtime config, which will make proxy use static fallback routing; (B) patch the rule parser to short-circuit nils, but that's riskier under load. recommend A for immediate relief.

Eva R: CS reports 3 paying customers in EU hitting degraded responses — one reported request truncation and another saw mismatched model variants (returned embeddings from small-v2). Need communication plan if we fail-open.

Maya K: agreed. I'll flip the flag and notify customers. Liam, please verify that the fail-open path won't loop.

Liam W: executing now:
```bash
# toggle feature flag in config store
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  https://config.internal/api/flags/policy-eval -d '{"enabled": false}'
# wait for propagation to runtime pools
```

sre-bot: [action] feature_flag_change recorded by Liam W at 2024-04-27T14:12:10Z flag=policy-eval old=true new=false

Liam W: flag is flipped. hitting /health on policy-engine instances shows 200 but route proxy logs show fallback routing now. I still see region imbalance — some proxies are aggressively sending to eu-fallback which is saturated.

Arjun Patel: I suspect the fallback policy had a buggy target selector that included both region and variant, and because we briefly had mismatched meta it created a tight loop. I'll patch the selector to prefer nearest-region with capacity and add a cooldown. deploying quick patch to routing-config.

Maya K: ETA?

Arjun Patel: pushing a targeted change to config-service: hotpatch routing-config/key=smart-fallback -> set prefer_nearest=true and cooldown_ms=500. CLI: 
```json
{"prefer_nearest": true, "cooldown_ms": 500}
```
should take effect within 30s.

sre-bot: [deploy] config-change queued by Arjun Patel -> routing-config.smart-fallback, deployment_id=cfg-9921

Liam W: starting to see metrics normalize. 502 rate trending down, CPU on eu-fallback decreasing. still some customers in EU reporting higher latencies (tail p95).

Eva R: reaching out to impacted accounts: writing initial blurb — "We're investigating elevated latency and transient errors affecting inference in EU. We have applied a temporary routing change to stabilize traffic and are working on a fix. We'll share updates every 30 minutes."

Maya K: good. we'll keep page open until p95 returns near baseline and error budget impact estimated.

Liam W: dug further into rule that triggered panic — it used an `in` operator but the runtime expects a list literal or set, not a dynamic expression. The malformed rule came from the UI when the rule author pasted a CSV string for regions. example bad rule:
```
request.user_tier == "enterprise" && request.route.region in "us,eu"
```
should have been:
```
request.user_tier == "enterprise" && request.route.region in ["us","eu"]
```
I have a followup PR to make the parser validate types and return parse errors instead of producing a nil AST node.

Arjun Patel: can you open a rollback/patch PR and block the current rule rollout? Also add a lint check in the admin UI to prevent submission of non-list to 'in'.

Liam W: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/policy/PR-4723 — adds validation + defensive eval. will also add a migration to mark the bad rule as disabled in config-store.

sre-bot: [pager] oncall handoff scheduled — Maya K -> next oncall Liam W at 15:00 UTC.

Maya K: handing off now. current state: policy-eval disabled, routing-config hotpatch applied, p95 down from 1.6s to 420ms, 502s reduced by 84% in the last 10m. customer impact: ~4% of requests in EU were affected during peak, several enterprise customers experienced latency spikes and one observed truncated embeddings. next steps for oncall: monitor for 30-60m, validate PR patch in staging, prepare post-incident customer note.

Liam W: acknowledged. I'll follow up with the parser fix, add UI validation, and coordinate a controlled re-enable once staging looks good.

Eva R: I'll draft a customer status with timeline and mitigation actions. put me in loop for quotes.

Maya K: closing pager here but keeping thread pinned for postmortem. please add any logs/snippets to the incident doc. thanks all. :thumbsup:
